newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea representatives deny defection.
newsitem.headline: North Korea representatives deny defection.

text.p: North Korean representatives in Japan on Wednesday denied reports that a senior North Korean aide had defected to the South, saying the official was due to arrive in Pyongyang on Thursday afternoon.

"We confirmed with the North Korean embassy in Beijing, as well as back home (in Pyongyang), that Secretary Hwang left Beijing for Pyongyang," O Huyong-jin, Vice Chairman of the General Association of Korean Residents in Japan said, referring to Hwang Jang-yop, a secretary in North Korea's ruling Workers' Party.

Hwang and three other North Korean officials took a train that left Beijing on Wednesday afternoon and were due to cross the border into North Korea at around noon on Thursday, he told a hastily-called news conference in Tokyo.
The South Korean government said earlier on Wednesday that Hwang and another North Korean had sought asylum at the South Korean embassy in China.

The General Association of Korean Residents in Japan is the de facto embassy of North Korea in Japan. Last week the association hosted a 13-day visit by Hwang to Japan. He left Tokyo for Beijing on Tuesday.
O Huyong-jin said Pyongyang should release a statement on the issue later on Wednesday or on Thursday.
He did not identify what source in Pyongyang had confirmed Hwang's departure, saying only: "We have reliable sources."
"This is a serious, international problem. If what we say turns out to be true, as it surely will, it's going to be a major incident," O Huyong-jin said.

Hwang is one of 11 secretaries on the powerful secretariat of the Workers' Party. The secretariat includes Kim Jong-il, the son and political heir of North Korean founder Kim Il-sung, who died in July 1994.
